youtube.title: America Set Off a Hydrogen Bomb in Space | Starfish Prime
youtube.description:
On 9 July 1962, the United States detonated a 1.4-megaton warhead about 250 miles above Johnston Island in the Pacific. Nearly 900 miles away in Hawaii, the sky lit up with an artificial aurora, about 300 streetlights went dark on Oahu, burglar alarms went off and a telephone link was knocked out. The radiation it left in orbit damaged satellites, including Telstar. A year later, the Limited Test Ban Treaty banned nuclear tests in space.

📂 Case File #017: Starfish Prime

Sources: The Space Review, "Starfish Prime"; Make Tech Easier, "In 1962, the US detonated a 1.4 megaton nuclear bomb 250 miles above the Pacific".
Images: Starfish Prime aurora from Honolulu, Johnston Island launch site, Johnston Atoll, Van Allen belts rendering (public domain, US government / NASA); Telstar model, CC BY-SA 3.0 FR (Wikimedia Commons).
Narration voice: AI.
